title: All-In-All-Out Pyrochlore Iridates as Noncollinear Spin-Orbit Coupled Counterparts of Altermagnets
authors: Yang Yang, Turan Birol, Rafael M. Fernandes, Natalia B. Perkins
abstract: Altermagnets are collinear magnetically ordered states that exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting in the absence of net magnetization and spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Related spin-splitting patterns, however, can also emerge in noncollinear magnetic systems with large SOC. Here we show, via a microscopic model, that the all-in-all-out (AIAO) state in pyrochlore iridates constitutes a noncollinear counterpart of a $d$-wave altermagnet stabilized by strong SOC. Starting from a microscopic $j_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1/2$ tight-binding model on the pyrochlore lattice, we demonstrate that electronic interactions favor the AIAO phase and analyze its symmetry properties. We show that the AIAO order parameter transforms as an $A_{2g}^{-}$ octupolar magnetic moment, breaking time-reversal symmetry while preserving inversion and zero net magnetization. Using group-theory analysis and mean-field calculations, we demonstrate that this symmetry enforces both a spin-polarized momentum-dependent lifting of band degeneracies that is similar to that of a collinear $d$-wave cubic altermagnet, but also a band splitting at zero-momentum. We show that the latter feature is captured by a low-energy model similar to the   Luttinger-Kohn model for cubic semiconductors. Our results identify pyrochlore iridates as a platform for noncollinear counterparts of altermagnetism and provide a general symmetry framework for spin-split phenomena in spin-orbit coupled materials.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates how the All-In-All-Out (AIAO) magnetic order in pyrochlore iridates realizes a noncollinear analogue of altermagnetism. Using microscopic models and group theory, it demonstrates that this specific octupolar ordering enforces unique symmetry constraints on the electronic band structure. This results in characteristic spin-polarized band splittings at both finite momentum and zero momentum ($\Gamma$ point).
main_problem: To determine if noncollinear magnetic orders can realize the momentum-dependent spin splitting characteristic of altermagnets in strongly SOC materials.
main_result: The All-In-All-Out (AIAO) state in pyrochlore iridates acts as a noncollinear counterpart to $d$-wave altermagnets, exhibiting both momentum-dependent and zero-momentum band splitting due to symmetry constraints.
method: The study employs microscopic tight-binding models combined with rigorous group-theory analysis and mean-field calculations to analyze the electronic structure under specific magnetic symmetries.
model_or_system: The system is pyrochlore iridates ($	ext{A}_2	ext{Ir}_2	ext{O}_7$) featuring $	ext{Ir}^{4+}$ ions with strong SOC, modeled using a $j_{	ext{eff}} = 1/2$ tight-binding Hamiltonian on the pyrochlore lattice.
key_observables: Spin-splitting patterns in electronic bands (pseudospin splitting), local magnetization density ($\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{r})$) decomposed into multipole moments, and symmetry constraints derived from magnetic space groups.
important_parameters: Strong Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC), the AIAO order parameter transforming as an $	ext{A}_{	ext{g}}^{-2	ext{g}}$ octupolar moment, and hopping parameters ($t, t'$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes strong SOC leading to $j_{	ext{eff}} = 1/2$ physics, and utilizes mean-field approximations for the electronic structure calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the AIAO magnetic configuration on a tetrahedron, compare band structures (non-magnetic vs. ordered), show local magnetization density isosurfaces with multipole decomposition, and present low-energy effective Hamiltonians derived from symmetry constraints.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical model and the AIAO state's symmetry properties; it then uses group theory to derive the symmetry-allowed low-energy Hamiltonian in the $\Gamma_{10}$ subspace; finally, it calculates the resulting electronic band structure splitting and the real-space multipolar character of the magnetic order.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework linking complex noncollinear magnetism (octupolar moments) to observable electronic signatures like momentum-dependent band splittings, which is crucial for understanding correlated topological materials.
